topics.topic_label: EU AI Act enforcement (the Commission's AI Office started enforcing on 2 August and the sharpest read is that the Code of Practice underneath is an engineering spec, not a legal text — written by someone who understands what an agent is, applying directly to only five to fifteen systemic-risk providers but flowing downhill from customers to suppliers; the DACH correction is now on the record twice, provider versus deployer and watermark versus visible notice)

Context engineering (the man who coined the term now says it is the wrong frame — Dex Horthy pushes past context engineering to harness and loop engineering, the durable leverage being the wrapper around the model rather than the prompt; and the failure mode gets named precisely on LinkedIn, an explicit guardrail surviving until the conversation grows long enough that summarisation renders it vague)

EU AI Act (the AI Office's GPAI enforcement powers went live 2 August with fines to EUR 15M or 3% of global turnover, and five separate Pulse pieces in one day work the same seam - Article 14 oversight is a legal specification rather than a slogan, Article 50 binds deployers regardless of risk class, existing observability traces already satisfy much of the logging duty, and autonomy does not move responsibility from the company to the agent)

Context engineering (the frame is being renamed in real time - three of today's Medium pieces on it argue the durable layer is the harness rather than the context window: compress conversation history, offload large tool results to a filesystem instead of the prompt, isolate subagent context, keep a retrieval path back to the original evidence; the topic's own territory is being annexed by 'AI control plane')

EU AI Act (enforcement operative since 2 August — the AI Office can demand technical documentation from GPAI providers, evaluate models, require risk mitigations and levy fines up to €15M or 3% of global turnover, while the Digital Omnibus deferred high-risk obligations to Dec 2027 / Aug 2028 but left prohibitions and transparency duties on the original date; the underdiscussed vector is that any third party, competitors included, can file a complaint a national authority is then obliged to act on)

Context engineering (LangChain publishes concrete thresholds instead of generalities — tool responses over 20,000 tokens offloaded to the filesystem and replaced with a path plus a 10-line preview, old write/edit arguments truncated to file pointers at 85% of the window, summarization only when offloading is exhausted; the transferable idea is the eval methodology, deliberately triggering compression at 10-25% of the window to manufacture enough events to compare implementations, with goal drift as the worst failure mode)
